premise: Choosing not to patent the polio vaccine to ensure maximum global distribution and access.
hook: He had the chance to become one of the wealthiest scientists in history, but gave it all away with a single question.
key_facts: Led the research team that developed the first successful polio vaccine in the early 1950s.
Announced on national radio in 1955 that the vaccine would not be patented.
Famously asked 'Would you patent the sun?' when questioned about ownership.
Contributed to the near-global eradication of wild poliovirus.

premise: From losing both parents in Delhi to becoming the biggest movie star in global cinema without a film-industry family background.
hook: He arrived in Mumbai with a suitcase and a promise to his dying mother that he would conquer the city.
key_facts: Lost both parents at a young age before establishing his career.
Started in television before transitioning to Bollywood villain roles.
Achieved global superstardom without any family connections in the film industry.

premise: A self-taught mathematical genius from Erode who produced groundbreaking theorems without formal university training.
hook: A low-level shipping clerk mailed a notebook filled with impossible mathematical equations to a professor in Cambridge.
key_facts: Grew up in modest circumstances in Tamil Nadu and struggled through regular college due to an obsession with mathematics.
Worked as a clerk at the Madras Port Trust to support his family while pursuing mathematics independently.
Sent a letter containing unproven mathematical formulas to British mathematician G.H. Hardy in 1913.
Was invited to Trinity College, Cambridge, where he became a Fellow of the Royal Society.

premise: Rising from the chess clubs of southern India to become the undisputed World Chess Champion.
hook: He learned the rules of chess from his mother at age six in a house without a computer or grandmaster coach.
key_facts: Became India's first international chess grandmaster in 1988 at the age of 18
Won the FIDE World Chess Championship in 2000, becoming the first Indian to hold the title
Defended and retained the world championship title in 2007, 2008, 2010, and 2012
Awarded India's highest civilian sporting honor, the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, in 1991
